facts.raw_span: A 15-year-old boy with biopsy-proven Crohn disease
infiximab therapy (5 mg/kg subcutaneous injection every 8 weeks)
later switched to adalimumab (40-mg/0.8-mL subcutaneous injection every 2 weeks) due to disease relapse
Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids
Both lower eyelids were ectropic
Visual acuity was 20/20 OU
Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins
Diffuse conjunctival hyperemia
Rest of the ophthalmic examination was unremarkable

concepts.why: The patient has bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids with crusty plaques on the eyelid margins, which are characteristic findings of blepharitis.
The patient has ectropic lower eyelids, which is a characteristic finding of ectropion.
The patient has diffuse conjunctival hyperemia, which is a characteristic finding of conjunctivitis.
The patient has biopsy-proven Crohn disease and was initially on infliximab therapy, which is a characteristic treatment for Crohn disease.
The patient developed ocular inflammation while on adalimumab therapy, which is a known side effect of the medication.
The patient developed ocular inflammation while on infliximab therapy, which is a known side effect of the medication.
The patient's symptoms of scaly, thickened, and erythematous eyelids are similar to those found in psoriasis, which is an autoimmune disorder.
The patient's symptoms of conjunctival hyperemia and ectropion are similar to those found in rheumatoid arthritis, which is an autoimmune disorder.
It explains the normal visual acuity despite other ocular symptoms.
